🌙 Closing Edition | November 9, 2026

METALS REBOUND. TOMORROW BRINGS THE INFLATION TEST.
A softer dollar and retreating oil gave metals breathing room today. But the strongest signals came from the physical market.

☢️ URANIUM — Watch the pounds.
Cameco’s October long-term benchmark stands at $98/lb, versus $91.55 spot. Contract pricing continues to command a premium.

China’s Yangshan import premium hit a record $230/tonne. Shanghai exchange inventories fell more than 24% last week to just 33,848 tonnes.

Today, Codelco’s chairman warned production would keep falling without private partners developing new projects. A reminder of how difficult replacing supply has become.

🥈 SILVER — Another positive session.
Front-month COMEX futures settled at $52.564, up 1.47%, their highest settlement since October 28. The rebound is building, with tomorrow’s inflation report the next test.

🥇 GOLD — Back above $4,100.
December futures settled at $4,114.50, up 1%. Softer oil eased inflation concerns, while a weaker dollar supported buying.

China also added approximately 25.8 tonnes to its official gold reserves in October—the largest monthly addition in three years.

👀 NEXT: US CPI tomorrow at 8:30 a.m. ET.
A cooler reading could support the rebound. A hotter print could revive pressure from the dollar and interest-rate expectations.

My take: CPI can move metals in minutes. Bringing new mines into production takes years.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily pulse.

Over the weekend I’ve been digging deeper into Mezzanine and am growing increasingly more bullish. I’ve deposited 10k+ of my own funds into the protocol and it’s earning an excellent yield + generating points which I suspect will become quite valuable too in due time.

A bunch of reasons why I am bullish:

 1) The founder, @phtevenstrong, is a true OG in the defi space and has been around for years. He knows how to find the best yields and put together innovative strategies and find edges in places others don’t think to look. He has a great reputation and a lot of connections in the space.

 2) This isn’t some app that has been vibe-coded over a weekend, the first public post was made back in February (https://t.co/beNSZ3Wl20), and they’ve been building in public all year.

 3) The tranches mechanism of allowing users to choose their own risk profile is genuinely interesting, and when coupled with tapping into RWAs for yield generation creates an opportunity not found anywhere else on the market.

 4) It’s early with only ~$5m TVL and one vault so your points per capital deployed ratio is going to be very high. I suspect the TVL is going to grow rapidly as more people discover the platform and more vaults are deployed. I believe they’re aiming for 2-3 per month.

 5) It has some people I really respect as seed investors, like @rektdiomedes who said it’s the first seed investment he’s made in three years (https://t.co/eUkEdprKTn)

 6) They can explain where the yield is coming from and are hyper transparent about everything, see this post to understand how they’re generating yield for their first vault, The Hastra Optimizer (https://t.co/XrjcSSkK8l) 

Yes I partnered with them to help spread the word and will receive some compensation for the whole deal, but I have partnered with many projects over the years and there aren’t that many that I am going and putting 5 figures of my own funds into (more than I’m receiving for our partnership) purely because I think it’s a great protocol and opportunity. With Mezzanine I think it’s a great opportunity.

It’s not without risks ofc, like anything in defi, so please dyor too and only put in funds that you’re comfortable with and that are appropriate for your portfolio and risk profile. 

But I really do recommend checking them out and at least keeping them on your radar. I suspect we’ll be hearing a lot more about Mezzanine in the coming months. This is another post I found which I think offers a really balanced and good perspective, and is also worth reading for those wanting to learn more: https://t.co/RlLh7SCRok.

If you want to sign up, you can use my ref link and you’ll earn a 10% bonus on any points you generate (and I will get a 10% bonus as well): https://t.co/hw0vyNvXcQ

In 10 years as CEO of two startups, I can't count how many times engineers pitched me a complete rewrite of our codebase.

It always reminded me of Steve Blank's Startup Suicide: Rewriting the Code and Joel Spolsky's Things You Should Never Do. Joel compared rewriting software from scratch to demolishing a building instead of renovating it. I always agreed and pushed back hard on rewrites.

But AI has completely changed my mind.

When you can coordinate a swarm of thousands of coding agents, the economics are completely different. Suddenly there's an enormous premium on having an agent-native codebase: super fast CI, minimal dependencies, clean architecture, every decision documented, and everything optimized for agents rather than humans.

For the first time in my career, I'm starting to think a complete rewrite might actually be the right call.

You REALLY can replace existing software with something that is much faster in performance, much cheaper to operate, as reliable (or more!) as before, with shockingly little effort when you know how to use AI

Expertise has never been this valuable!!

If you're building in AI, the most important thing to master is the economics of compute. My take: respect the GPU or the GPU will humble you.

We're in a compute shortage. A GB300 costs roughly $7/hour on the spot market so depending on the frontier model, that hour buys you some millions of output tokens.

The only question is: how much customer value can you create with those tokens?

If it's less than $7, you have a problem. Customer won't pay you, so you won't be able to afford more compute, and VCs can subsidize you forever. Eventually, someone who creates more value per GPU-hour will outbid you.

The same GPU-hour could be spent generating another meme or helping discover a cancer treatment. The economic value of those outputs is wildly different.

My take is that you have to design your entire product around this equation. What's the smallest model that can do the job? Can you batch the work? Run it asynchronously during off-peak hours? Avoid generating tokens you don't need?

Every architecture decision, every feature, every token changes your compute economics. The entire roadmap has to be decided for the compute equation. 

What's hard is that in traditional software eng, you could often treat compute as practically free but the agent era, compute is the most important constraint.

🚨 HBM5 Doubles Bandwidth Without Adding a Single Pin 🚨

HBM5 keeps the same 2048 pins as HBM4E and runs each one nearly 2× faster. Samsung's Hot Chips 2026 presentation shows pin speed going from 14 Gbps on HBM4E to over 28 Gbps on HBM5.

Faster pins are only half the story. To keep each pin fed, everything behind the pins doubles too: DRAM banks, TSVs, and an upgraded PHY on the base die.
